tools.name: search_listings
tools.description: Full-text search over The Agents Index's Published agents. Returns compact records (name, slug, tagline, url). Fetch depth with get_listing.

tools.name: get_listing
tools.description: One agent in full, as answer-first markdown: the summary, then every question on the sheet with its answer, the vendor's own words for it and the URL that proves it. Identical to /{slug}.md and to the HTML page.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The Agents Index's categories with their live listing counts, 0 for one with none yet.

tools.name: compare_listings
tools.description: Two agents side by side, as markdown: taglines, pricing, API availability, tags — the researched compare facts, honest about unknowns.

tools.name: get_best_of
tools.description: The Published agents in one category, in the order its category page prints (ranked by what we can confirm: a public price, an API and docs, independent sources, stated limits), as a markdown answer sheet. Payment never moves a row.

tools.name: submit_listing
tools.description: Submit an agent to The Agents Index: the url alone; we write its name and description from its own pages. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, submit_listing, my_listings · Private data: search_listings · Public sink: submit_listing, send_lead, my_listings, subscribe_newsletter.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, submit_listing, my_listings · Private data: search_listings · Public sink: submit_listing, send_lead, my_listings, subscribe_newsletter

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
